newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FOCUS - Czech CEZ posts sharply lower H1 results.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Czech CEZ posts sharply lower H1 results.

text.p: Czech power utility CEZ a.s. on Friday became the latest in a line of major Czech companies to post sharply lower first half profits.
CEZ said that, according to international accounting standards, its first half after-tax profit slumped to 3.5 billion crowns ($101.4 million) from 5.95 billion in the same period last year.
"Apart from the anticipated growth in costs the decline was also influenced by a fall in electricity sales," CEZ said in a statement accompanying the results.

The company added that electricity sales fell by one percent year-on-year in the first half to 26.4 billion crowns and that operating expenses rose 1.8 billion crowns, 9.8 percent, to 20.6 billion crowns.
Total revenues fell 1.2 percent to 28.2 billion crowns

Analysts, who this week have become accustomed to blue chip companies confounding already pessimistic predicitions with even worse than expected results, put CEZ's performance in the context of the downturn of the wider economy.

"After the recently published economic results of our biggest banking institutions, we can see that energy company CEZ is another whose half year results are negatively influenced by the continuing stagnation of the Czech economy," said Patrik Brom of Prague International Securities.
Growth in Czech gross domestic product slumped to 1.5 percent year-on-year in the first quarter of 1997 from 4.6 perecnt in the same period last year.
Eugene Klerk of ABN AMRO Hoare Govett focused on the heavy fall in second quarter profits.

"I had forecast second quarter profits of 1.47 billion crowns and second quarter profits actually came out at 690 million crowns...and that is almost something like 70 percent below second quarter profit of 1996."
"The figures look really bad ...again it shows that this company is going nowhere," he added.
In response to the news, CEZ shares lost ground on the Prague Stock Exchange, falling 13 crowns to 905 by mid-session during continuous trading.
RESULTS: for six month period ending June 30, 1997, to international accounting standards (in billions of crowns).
AFTER TAX PROFIT 3.53 5.95
PRE-TAX PROFIT 5.93 9.61
OPERATING PROFIT 7.53 9.72
OPERATING REVENUES 28.17 28.51
OPERATING EXPENSES 20.64 18.79
